prompt: Finish an expression tree by adding Mul and Sub subclasses of the provided abstract Expr, rendering each node with the fewest brackets that preserve its meaning -- including the case where a minus needs brackets around its right child but not its left.
explanation: Each node of the tree implements the same three abstract methods, so a parent can ask any child for its value, its precedence and its text without knowing which subclass it is -- that is polymorphism doing the recursion for you. The inherited renderChild helper brackets a child only when it binds more loosely than its parent, which is enough for the commutative operators. Subtraction is the exception: because a - (b - c) differs from (a - b) - c, its right child must be bracketed whenever it is an equally loose + or -, so Sub tightens the rule on that side only.
hints: Model Mul on the provided Add: two Expr fields, eval multiplying the children, precedence 2, and render using renderChild on both sides.
Sub has precedence 1 like Add, so renderChild alone will never bracket another + or - -- it only brackets children that are strictly looser.
In Sub.render, handle the right side yourself: bracket it when right.precedence() <= precedence(), and only fall back to renderChild otherwise. The left side can still use renderChild.
